title: Least squares inside bounds
prompt:
Estimate how far each of four CRAH valves is open (each between 0 and 1) from flow measurements: minimize ½‖Aw − b‖²/n subject to lo ≤ w ≤ hi, elementwise.

1. `bounded_lsq(A, b, lo, hi, iters=5000)` runs projected gradient from the midpoint of the box: a gradient step with step size 1/L (L = largest eigenvalue of AᵀA/n), then clipping into the bounds. Return w.
2. `kkt_residual(A, b, w, lo, hi)` returns the largest violation of the box KKT conditions at w, with g the gradient: for coordinates strictly inside the box, |gᵢ|; at a lower bound, max(0, −gᵢ); at an upper bound, max(0, gᵢ). (Treat |wᵢ − bound| < 1e-9 as "at" the bound.) Zero means optimal.
hints: A gradient step can push a coordinate outside its bounds. What's the closest point inside a box, coordinate by coordinate?

Projection onto a box is clipping each coordinate to its interval. At the optimum, a coordinate strictly inside has zero gradient; one stuck at its lower bound must have gᵢ ≥ 0 (decreasing it would help but isn't allowed) and one at its upper bound gᵢ ≤ 0.

w = np.clip((lo + hi) / 2, lo, hi); L = np.linalg.eigvalsh(A.T @ A / n).max(); repeat w = np.clip(w - (A.T @ (A @ w - b) / n) / L, lo, hi). KKT: g = A.T @ (A @ w - b) / n; at_lo = np.abs(w - lo) < 1e-9; at_hi = np.abs(w - hi) < 1e-9; inside = ~(at_lo | at_hi); return max of |g[inside]|, max(0, -g[at_lo]), max(0, g[at_hi]).

misconceptions.clip-after-fit: Clipping an unconstrained least-squares solution into the box is generally not the constrained optimum: once one coordinate is fixed at a bound, the others should move to compensate.
misconceptions.box-kkt-signs: At a lower bound the gradient must be non-negative, at an upper bound non-positive: the objective would improve only by leaving the box.
